text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn reached a decision with the leaders of the parliamentary parties on Wednesday not to dispatch Hungarian soldiers as part of an international peace-keeping force to Albania.
- Judges from the International Court of Judges in the Hague will cross into Hungary today to inspect the aborted hydroelectric power plant at Nagymaros.
- President Arpad Goncz arrived in Rio de Janeiro yesterday.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs signed an agreement on foreign ministerial cooperation in Egypt on Wednesday.

- Free Democrat leader has asked Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal to call on Smallholder MP Agnes Nagy Maczo to resign her post as deputy speaker today on account of her recent anti- Semitic remarks in Parliament.

- The government is to step up public investments by 20 percent in real terms next year, said Finance Ministry State Secretary Tibor Draskovics adding that inflation will be around 13 percent over the entire year of 1998.

- Although the independence and financial position of the National Bank of Hungary (MNB) has benefited from recent reforms, MNB and Finance Ministry plans to fight inflation may turn out to be ineffective, says a EU report published in Brussels yesterday.
- Three opposition parties jointly urged an immediate halt to the privatisation of MOL Rt. and the Hungarian Electricity Works and that of the energy sector as a whole.
- Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank won the tender of savings bank Takarekbank, fetching the highest price in the history of Hungarian privatisation.

- A senior Defence Ministry official announced Wednesday that the French company Matra Defense has won the first major tender launched by the Ministry's Procurement Office for low altitude air defence missile systems.

- Lockheed Martin Corp. President and General Manager Norman R. Augustine suggested in Budapest Wednesday that East European countries hoping to gain NATO membership should club together to procure fighter planes.

- Former Hungarian soccer ace Ferenc Puskas received a Gold Memorial Medal and a golden soccer ball on the occasion of his 70th birthday Wednesday. Puskas was also awarded a gold memorial medal by IOC chief Juan Antonio Samaranch.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Gypsies and ethnic Germans in Hungary put forward the most legal grievances against the police, according to Jeno Kaltenbach, ombudsman for minority rights.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Spanish government sources indicated Wednesday that the US and Spain agreed Tuesday to invite Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic to the NATO summit meeting in Madrid in July.
- The Israeli finance minister will visit Hungary next month to hold talks on the possibility of a free trade agreement, announced Israeli Ambassador Joel Alon.
- The holding Fotex Rt. has successfully issued 343 bonds to institutional investors.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- At Slovenia's proposal the defence ministers of Slovenia, Italy and Hungary will meet in Ljubljana on Friday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Wednesday saw the opening of the Budapest office of Utell International, the world's largest hotel reservation firm.
